correctness.rationale: The facet description follows from the single circuit-hyperplane rank inequality, and the circuit facet is the product of two triangles. The exact normal lattice, six square primitive-ray relations and ten rank-five exchange cones determine all smooth/nonsmooth orbits. Orbit-face closure incidence yields exactly six planar components meeting on a 3-by-3 grid plus ten isolated components. Complete arithmetic enumeration of all 285 faces and cone saturation tests corroborates the structural derivation. Local toric semigroup presentations prove conifold and 3-by-3 rank-one Segre cone types and multiplicities 2 and 6.

value.rationale: The smallest nonuniform single-circuit-hyperplane rank-three matroid gives a natural singularity test for a one-facet hypersimplex split. Its complete toric singularity geometry consists of an unexpected six-plane K3,3 incidence pattern alongside ten isolated Segre cone singularities; distinguishing these local models and multiplicities is structural information not encoded by the already-known face vector and relevant for toric intersection/birational problems.
